items.summary: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question.

items.author: Ivan Klaric

items.title: The next developer interface is ambient intelligence
items.author: Martin Woodward
items.description: AI, agents, voice, and physical controls are shifting software development from operating tools to expressing intent—and helping developers stay focused on building. The post The next developer interface is ambient intelligence appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.summary: For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools changed, but the relationship did not.

items.summary: Working with outside collaborators can add more work for a repository owner. You need to confirm who still needs access, change permissions as projects evolve, and archive repositories once they’ve served their purpose.

items.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
items.author: Taylor Cuilty
items.description: Our new repo star history API now provides trends without returning individual identities or requiring unbounded database work. These are the engineering tradeoffs we made. The post From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.summary: Maintainers look at star history to answer a practical question: did a launch, release, or event change a project’s trajectory? To reconstruct that curve from the GitHub API, tools had to request pages of stargazer records (each person who currently stars the repository and when they starred it), keep the timestamps, and throw the identities away.

items.title: Do You Trust Apple?

items.description: Apple has a lot of trust in terms of delivering integrated products and preserving privacy; the real trust question is if you think Siri AI will justify investing more in their ecosystem.

items.title: How I AI: Meta Muse Wonder + How Brooke Lacey is scaling video with AI
items.author: Lenny Rachitsky
items.description: Your weekly listens from How I AI, part of the Lenny's Podcast Network

She also shares how Muse compares with Opus 5.5, Astra, and Fable, and why she plans to test it in a few agent workflows without letting it anywhere near her front end.

items.summary: Reconstructing human activity from egocentric video requires more than recovering individual 3D components: the observer's motion, surrounding geometry, and hand-object interactions must fit together in a consistent world. items.summary: Lifelong agents continually accumulate and reuse experience to improve after deployment, yet in practice they often operate under tight generation, interaction, and memory budgets.
